title: Sr. Scientist - Proteomics Informatics & Computational Biology

cond_0001.intro: The Proteomics Informatics Senior Scientist will be a key member of the Discovery Mass Spectrometry Team, enabling the analysis, at scale, of highly complex datasets generated by proteomic and other omic technologies to drive biomarker discovery and reagent characterization. The role will require a deep understanding of mass spectrometry-based data, especially protein- and proteomics-based data, together with advanced computational and bioinformatic skills. We are looking for a team player who is collaborative with strong communication skills.
cond_0001.responsibilities:
What You Can Expect
You will be an integral part of a dynamic mass spectrometry team that develops, characterizes and supports novel and robust multiomic biomarker assays. You will utilize data from cutting edge instrumentation to analyze proteomic, metabolomic and lipidomic experiments across blood, urine, tissue and fecal samples. You will drive development of data processing workflows for large biomarker discovery experiments, including proteogenomic and spatial omic workflows. You will document code, experiments and other activities. Prepare reports and summaries. Present results and conclusions. You will interface with multiple cross-functional teams to support discovery and new product development. You will communicate and clearly present results to a broad audience within R&D, including [Company name masked] senior leadership.
cond_0001.requirements:
Minimum Requirements
Degree in computational biology, bioinformatics, computer science, or a related technical field.
PhD with 0-2 years of experience or MS with 0-5 years of experience or equivalent combination of education and experience.
Strong background in mass spectrometry-based omics data analysis and interpretation, such as proteomics, metabolomics, lipidomics, proteogenomics.
Proficiency in programming languages such as Python or R and experience with bioinformatic tools as well as tools such as git, Jupyter notebooks, Streamlit.
Hands-on experience with and demonstrated understanding of mass spectrometry and proteomic software tools.
Excellent communication and organizational skills.
Ability to work independently, as well as collaboratively, in a team environment.
Preferred Requirements
Experience working in cloud-based and mixed computing environments, including AWS, GCE, Snowflake, etc.
Detail-oriented and ability to adapt quickly to changing priorities.
Ability to take initiative and be accountable.
Demonstrated ability to critically evaluate techniques and results and implement improved practices.
If you're looking for a role that'll challenge you, offer a variety of work and learning, while helping an amazing industry, we'd love to hear from you!

cond_0063.intro: The Proteomics Informatics Senior Scientist will be a core member of the Discovery Mass Spectrometry Team, working alongside colleagues to support the analysis, at scale, of highly complex datasets generated by proteomic and other omic technologies. Together, the team works to advance biomarker discovery and reagent characterization. The role requires a deep understanding of mass spectrometry-based data, especially protein- and proteomics-based data, along with strong computational and bioinformatic skills. We are looking for someone who works well with others and communicates clearly.

You will collaborate with teammates to analyze proteomic, metabolomic, and lipidomic experiments across blood, urine, tissue, and fecal samples using data from cutting-edge instrumentation. You will coordinate with the team on the development of data processing workflows for large biomarker discovery experiments, including proteogenomic and spatial omic workflows. You will document code, experiments, and other activities. Prepare reports and summaries. Present results and conclusions. You will work alongside multiple cross-functional teams to support discovery and new product development. You will share results clearly with a broad audience within R&D, including [Company name masked] senior leadership.

The role requires a deep understanding of mass spectrometry-based data, especially protein- and proteomics-based data, along with strong computational and bioinformatic skills. We are looking for someone who works well with others and communicates clearly.
cond_0279.responsibilities: You will work as part of a mass spectrometry team that develops, characterizes, and supports novel and robust multiomic biomarker assays. You will collaborate with teammates to analyze proteomic, metabolomic, and lipidomic experiments across blood, urine, tissue, and fecal samples using data from cutting-edge instrumentation. You will coordinate with the team on the development of data processing workflows for large biomarker discovery experiments, including proteogenomic and spatial omic workflows. You will document code, experiments, and other activities. Prepare reports and summaries. Present results and conclusions. You will work alongside multiple cross-functional teams to support discovery and new product development. You will share results clearly with a broad audience within R&D, including [Company name masked] senior leadership.
cond_0279.requirements:
Minimum Requirements
Degree in computational biology, bioinformatics, computer science, or a related technical field
PhD with 0–2 years of experience, or MS with 0–5 years of experience, or equivalent combination of education and experience
Strong background in mass spectrometry-based omics data analysis and interpretation, such as proteomics, metabolomics, lipidomics, or proteogenomics
Proficiency in Python or R, and experience with bioinformatic tools as well as tools such as git, Jupyter notebooks, and Streamlit
Hands-on experience with and demonstrated understanding of mass spectrometry and proteomic software tools
Excellent communication and organizational skills
Preferred Requirements
Experience working in cloud-based and mixed computing environments, including AWS, GCE, Snowflake, etc.
Detail-oriented with the ability to adapt quickly to changing priorities
Ability to work independently as well as collaboratively in a team environment
Ability to take initiative and be accountable
Demonstrated ability to critically evaluate techniques and results and implement improved practices
If you're looking for a role that'll challenge you, offer a variety of work and learning, while helping an amazing industry, we'd love to hear from you!

cond_0302.intro: The Proteomics Informatics Senior Scientist will be a member of the Discovery Mass Spectrometry Team, enabling the analysis, at scale, of highly complex datasets generated by proteomic and other omic technologies to support biomarker discovery and reagent characterization. The role requires a deep understanding of mass spectrometry-based data, especially protein- and proteomics-based data, together with advanced computational and bioinformatic skills. We are looking for a team player who is collaborative with strong communication skills. People usually grow into this role over time as they build experience with proteomics data analysis and computational workflows.
cond_0302.responsibilities: You will be an integral part of a mass spectrometry team that develops, characterizes and supports novel and robust multiomic biomarker assays. You will utilize data from cutting edge instrumentation to analyze proteomic, metabolomic and lipidomic experiments across blood, urine, tissue and fecal samples. You will drive development of data processing workflows for large biomarker discovery experiments, including proteogenomic and spatial omic workflows. You will document code, experiments and other activities. Prepare reports and summaries. Present results and conclusions. You will interface with multiple cross-functional teams to support discovery and new product development. You will communicate and clearly present results to a broad audience within R&D, including [Company name masked] senior leadership.
cond_0302.requirements: Degree in computational biology, bioinformatics, computer science, or a related technical field. PhD with 0-2 years of experience or MS with 0-5 years of experience or equivalent combination of education and experience. Strong background in mass spectrometry-based omics data analysis and interpretation, such as proteomics, metabolomics, lipidomics, proteogenomics. Proficiency in programming languages such as Python or R and experience with bioinformatic tools as well as tools such as git, Jupyter notebooks, Streamlit. Experience working in cloud-based and mixed computing environments, including AWS, GCE, Snowflake, etc. Hands-on experience with and demonstrated understanding of mass spectrometry and proteomic software tools. Detail-oriented and ability to adapt quickly to changing priorities. Excellent communication and organizational skills. Ability to work independently, as well as collaboratively, in a team environment. Ability to take initiative and be accountable. Demonstrated ability to critically evaluate techniques and results and implement improved practices.

cond_0349.intro: The Proteomics Informatics Senior Scientist will be a member of the Discovery Mass Spectrometry Team, supporting analysis, at scale, of highly complex datasets generated by proteomic and other omic technologies to support biomarker discovery and reagent characterization. The role requires a deep understanding of mass spectrometry-based data, especially protein- and proteomics-based data, together with advanced computational and bioinformatic skills.
cond_0349.responsibilities:
You will be part of a mass spectrometry team that develops, characterizes and supports novel and robust multiomic biomarker assays.
You will use data from cutting edge instrumentation to analyze proteomic, metabolomic and lipidomic experiments across blood, urine, tissue and fecal samples.
You will develop data processing workflows for large biomarker discovery experiments, including proteogenomic and spatial omic workflows.
You will document code, experiments and other activities.
Prepare reports and summaries.
Share results and conclusions with relevant stakeholders.
You will coordinate with multiple cross-functional teams as required to support discovery and new product development.
You will document and share results with R&D stakeholders, including [Company name masked] senior leadership.
cond_0349.requirements:
Minimum Requirements
Degree in computational biology, bioinformatics, computer science, or a related technical field
PhD with 0-2 years of experience, or MS with 0-5 years of experience, or equivalent combination of education and experience
Strong background in mass spectrometry-based omics data analysis and interpretation, such as proteomics, metabolomics, lipidomics, proteogenomics
Proficiency in programming languages such as Python or R, and experience with bioinformatic tools as well as tools such as git, Jupyter notebooks, Streamlit
Hands-on experience with and demonstrated understanding of mass spectrometry and proteomic software tools
Demonstrated ability to critically evaluate techniques and results and implement improved practices
Preferred Requirements
Experience working in cloud-based and mixed computing environments, including AWS, GCE, Snowflake, etc.
Detail-oriented with ability to adapt to changing priorities
Strong written communication and clear, direct verbal reporting
Ability to work independently and within a team
Ability to take initiative and be accountable

The role will require a deep understanding of mass spectrometry-based data, especially protein- and proteomics-based data, together with advanced computational and bioinformatic skills. We are looking for a team player who is collaborative with strong communication skills.
cond_0488.responsibilities:
What You Can Expect
You will be an integral part of a dynamic mass spectrometry team that develops, characterizes and supports novel and robust multiomic biomarker assays. You will utilize data from cutting edge instrumentation to analyze proteomic, metabolomic and lipidomic experiments across blood, urine, tissue and fecal samples. You will drive development of data processing workflows for large biomarker discovery experiments, including proteogenomic and spatial omic workflows. You will document code, experiments and other activities. Prepare reports and summaries. Present results and conclusions. You will interface with multiple cross-functional teams to support discovery and new product development. You will communicate and clearly present results to a broad audience within R&D, including [Company name masked] senior leadership.
cond_0488.requirements:
Minimum Requirements
Degree in computational biology, bioinformatics, computer science, or a related technical field; PhD with 0–2 years of demonstrated expertise or MS with 0–5 years of demonstrated expertise, or equivalent combination of education and experience.
Extensive background in mass spectrometry-based omics data analysis and interpretation, including proteomics, metabolomics, lipidomics, and proteogenomics.
Deep expertise in programming languages such as Python or R, along with strong command of bioinformatic tools and tools such as git, Jupyter notebooks, and Streamlit.
Proven track record working in cloud-based and mixed computing environments, including AWS, GCE, Snowflake, or similar platforms.
Substantial hands-on expertise with mass spectrometry and proteomic software tools, with a demonstrated advanced understanding of their application.
Preferred Requirements
Exceptional communication and organizational skills, with the ability to present complex results clearly to a broad audience.
Demonstrated ability to work independently and collaboratively, with strong initiative and accountability.
Detail-oriented with the ability to adapt quickly to changing priorities.
Demonstrated ability to critically evaluate techniques and results and implement improved practices.
